Early game, only Vermont owned, $1400 cash. No trades worth making — opponents own nothing. Don't mortgage. End turn and look to complete light blue (Oriental/Connecticut) or pick up high-value unowned properties next rolls.

Orange is the highest-EV monopoly (Jail adjacency). $180 is cheap relative to $1406 cash and rent curve. Own 0/3 but denying opponents and starting the set is clearly +EV. Auction risks handing it to someone cheap. p4 already blocks light blue with Connecticut; pivot toward orange while Oriental remains a later option. Buy.

No monopoly, nothing to build or mortgage. Opponents only hold Reading, Electric, and Connecticut. Connecticut blocks light blue but p4 just bought it and won't trade cheap. No useful trade. End and keep cash for orange (TN/NY) or remaining high-value landings.

No monopoly, nothing to build. $1426 cash, Vermont + St. James. Light blue blocked by p4's Connecticut and Oriental still bank-owned, so buying Connecticut now doesn't complete a set. Oranges (TN/NY) still unowned — better to keep cash and land them than overpay p4. No mortgage needed. End turn.
